route_b_numpy_lanes.how_the_bar_was_raised: the brief's 1e-12 comes from vectorised np.interp being UNFUSED (hazard 6). That was not accepted. cablp/numerics/interp.py gained interp_array_fused, whose interior lerp goes through fma_array -- an exact reconstruction of math.fma from Dekker's two-product, Knuth's two-sum, and a ROUND-TO-ODD tail before the closing add. numpy has no FMA ufunc and its x86-64 baseline does not contract a*b+c, so the single rounding is rebuilt rather than emitted.
route_b_numpy_lanes.why_this_matters: at rel 1e-12 this member would MOVE THE GOLDEN (an anchor event, a reviewed recapture) and would force scripts/deposit_beam_reference.py -- a raw-uint64 fixture over 206,218 values -- to be downgraded to a tolerance comparison. At bitwise 0 it moves nothing and the fixture keeps its teeth. The cost of the reconstruction is about 20 numpy ops per lerp, and it is the single largest term in the round; it is what caps the speedup reported below.
route_b_numpy_lanes.cost_of_the_bar: measured. The three per-round lookups were batched into ONE fused multiply-add (and, where two share a grid, one bracketing search); that bought 5%. The exact-FMA reconstruction is not removable without giving up the bar.

route_proposal.third_option_considered_and_rejected: np.interp verbatim (the brief's literal route (b)). Rejected on the two consequences above, not on difficulty.

hazard_gates.how_addressed: each lane evaluates its own dz_sub from its own E and its own remaining; a round advances every active lane by one of ITS substeps, never by a shared one. No leg cap exists. frac is threaded from the caller.
hazard_gates.evidence: substeps_top/substeps_nested/legs reproduce on all 506 corpus entries; per-lane substep counts match a hooked recursive count on 5,690 randomized lanes.

hazard_gates.isa_contraction_consequence_stated: FP contraction is an ISA-baseline property: aarch64 fuses a*b+c, numpy's x86-64 baseline does not. Had the vectorised lerp been left to numpy's own arithmetic, the answer would have depended on which machine built numpy -- the exact defect interp_scalar_fused was created to close. The reconstruction removes that dependence by CONSTRUCTION on both routes, so this member adds no new platform-dependent site. -ffp-contract=off remains correct for the compiled path and is untouched.

corrections_and_addenda.raised_by: reviewer finding at the lane-march merge; dispatched as its own single-purpose member under the house loud-over-silent rule.
corrections_and_addenda.base_revision: e95bb21 (agent-staging tip after the lane-march merge). The worktree spawned STALE on campaign 39cb395 and was reset --hard onto e95bb21 before anything was written.
corrections_and_addenda.finding: fma_array's docstring claimed unconditional bit-identity with math.fma. It is bit-identical EXCEPT when the product a*b underflows into the subnormal window, which check_fma_domain did not fence -- it bounded only the overflow ceiling FMA_ARRAY_MAX_ABS. Reproduced at raw uint64 on triples whose product is forced below 2**-970: 64,599 of 300,000 differ when the addend exposes the residual (c = -a*b), 3,595 of 300,000 on an independently drawn addend. The rate is a property of the probe; what the defect asserts is that it is not zero.
corrections_and_addenda.root_cause: Dekker's two-product is error-free only ABSENT UNDERFLOW. The precondition is on the factors' exponents, e_a + e_b >= e_min + p - 1 (Muller et al., Handbook of Floating-Point Arithmetic, 2nd ed. 4.4.1), i.e. |a*b| >= 2**(-1022 + 53 - 1) = 2**-970 ~ 1.0021e-292. Below it the split partial products round in the subnormal range, the residual e stops being the whole rounding error of a*b, and the reconstruction silently double-rounds.
corrections_and_addenda.the_fence: check_fma_domain gains a LOWER fence, FMA_ARRAY_MIN_ABS, on every NONZERO element of the MULTIPLIED operands. Exact zeros are exempt (0*x is exactly 0). The addend c is exempt via a new keyword-only argument factor=True: c reaches the answer only through Knuth's two-sum, which is error-free for any finite operands, and a subnormal addend measures 0 differing over 300,000 triples -- fencing it would refuse a call the reconstruction handles exactly. The ValueError names the precondition ('the Dekker two-product is error-free only absent underflow') and the measured reachable margin.
corrections_and_addenda.derived_bound: FMA_ARRAY_MIN_ABS = 1e-145, from the requirement MIN**2 >= ~1e-290: the product of two fenced nonzero operands is then at least 1e-290, clearing the 2**-970 = 1.0021e-292 exactness threshold by 99.8x. Veltkamp's splitter cannot underflow on it either (_SPLITTER * 1e-145 ~ 1.3e-137). The value mirrors the ceiling -- 1e150**2 = 1e300 stays finite exactly as 1e-145**2 = 1e-290 stays normal. NON-BINDING by 122 decades on everything reachable: over the committed deposit_beam corpus plus 2,000 randomized lane batteries (147,764 fma calls, 5,889,066 operand elements) the smallest nonzero operand magnitude is 4.657572e-23 and the smallest nonzero |a*b| is 9.448888e-28, 265 decades above the threshold.
